    <item>
      <title>LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch</link>
      <description><p>At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports</p><p>Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a <a href="https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/10/12/senegal-brutal-crackdown-violates-lgbt-peoples-rights">new report</a>.</p><p>More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, <a href="https://www.hivjustice.net/cases/senegal-crackdown-on-lgbtq-people-intensifies-with-multiple-arrests/">according to HIV Justice Network</a>, an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch">Continue reading...</a></description>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/global-development">Global development</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/senegal">Senegal</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/lgbt-rights">LGBTQ+ rights</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/human-rights">Human rights</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/law/human-rights">Human rights</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/anti-rights-movement">Anti-rights movement</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/africa">Africa</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/world">World news</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/law/law">Law</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/society/aids-and-hiv">Aids and HIV</category>
      <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 08:00:25 GMT</pubDate>
      <guid>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch</guid>
      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5d08247e565b832f183d37b676fe7def25b19c25/213_0_2500_2000/master/2500.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=123bd8ecc615f6c5a01371cef3492c23">
        <media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Photograph: Jane Hahn/AP</media:credit>

      <title>Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial</link>
      <description><p>Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/guinea-bissau">Guinea-Bissau</a> has not approved the controversial <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/hepatitis-b">hepatitis B</a> study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday.</p><p>The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Recommended dose of hepatitis B vaccine will be withheld from thousands of newborns by Danish researchers</p><p>A controversial research trial that will withhold hepatitis B vaccines from some African newborns was given approval to move forward this week.</p><p>It is a central part of the vaccine vision for Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime vaccine opponent.</p><p>This article was amended on 13 October 2026.       <title>ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize</link>
      <description><p>Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza</p><p></p><p>The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/sep/16/israel-committed-genocide-in-gaza-says-un-inquiry">that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza</a>.</p><p>The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the international court of justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>en</language><title>France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines</title><description>Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 14:45:15 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Sport</category><title>South African rugby player found dead in French hotel ahead of Champions Cup debut</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/sport/20261016-south-african-rugby-player-found-dead-in-french-hotel-ahead-of-champions-cup-debut</link><description>
A South African rugby player for the Lions team was found dead at a hotel in France Friday on the eve of a European Champions Cup game with ​La ‌Rochelle, local media reported. The player's identity has yet not been made public.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19fbab88-c95e-11f1-9346-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/000-936A662.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19fbab88-c95e-11f1-9346-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/000-936A662.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ee4f665a-c962-11f1-a6d8-9f93f5a64840</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 13:40:05 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19fbab88-c95e-11f1-9346-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/000-936A662.jpg">© Romain Perrocheau, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Africa</category><title>Ethiopia announces interim government in Tigray, aims for polls in six months</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20261016-ethiopia-announces-interim-government-tigray-calls-for-polls-six-months</link><description>
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on Friday announced the appointment of an interim administration to prepare elections in the northern Tigray region previously controlled by the Tigray People's Liberation Front that has clashed with government forces since September. The recent conflict revived a war that killed hundreds of thousands between 2020 and 2022.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3f160318-c95f-11f1-8341-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26284531962755.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3f160318-c95f-11f1-8341-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26284531962755.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0a670ee4-c95c-11f1-9fa5-c16b5c3a9206</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 13:05:23 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3f160318-c95f-11f1-8341-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26284531962755.jpg">© Filmon Equar Hailu, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Pope Leo XIV celebrates mass in hospital while recovering from lung cancer operation</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261016-pope-leo-xiv-celebrates-mass-in-hospital-while-recovering-from-lung-cancer-operation</link><description>
Pope Leo XIV celebrated a mass at Rome's Gemelli hospital Friday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung, photos released by the Vatican showed. Doctors said his recovery was progressing normally but that further tests would show whether the cancer had spread.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20a78260-c961-11f1-a208-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/b9a198cac6936ae44ee5b8c08a3fe4152c41404a.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20a78260-c961-11f1-a208-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/b9a198cac6936ae44ee5b8c08a3fe4152c41404a.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">216586d4-c961-11f1-8b74-219ae52178dc</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 12:57:23 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20a78260-c961-11f1-a208-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/b9a198cac6936ae44ee5b8c08a3fe4152c41404a.jpg">© Vatican media handout via AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Talking Europe</category><title>'America, with this president, is not our ally. Trump is a liar': French MEP Bernard Guetta</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/talking-europe/20261016-america-with-this-president-is-not-our-ally-trump-is-a-liar-french-mep-bernard-guetta</link><description>
Our guest is veteran French journalist and commentator Bernard Guetta, who is a Member of the European Parliament for the centrist Renew group. He tells the programme that Donald Trump is "a liar, because he tried to tell the American people that Zelensky and the Ukrainian resistance were responsible for the price of diesel. This is a pure lie. He (Trump) is responsible because he started the war with Iran." Guetta goes on to say that "without American intelligence sharing, Ukraine is weaker and weaker. That's terrible, to see the president of the United States giving a hand to Putin against Ukraine."
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/54ceab9e-c8a4-11f1-b31f-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/ENTK-TALKING-EU1-GUETTA-261017-2027-Ep-7-transfer.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/54ceab9e-c8a4-11f1-b31f-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/ENTK-TALKING-EU1-GUETTA-261017-2027-Ep-7-transfer.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">15b7bc28-c653-11f1-8f3d-97eea9bcf669</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 12:55:38 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Armen GEORGIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Reporters</category><title>'Thanks a lot, Trump': Wyoming conservatives divided ahead of US midterms</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/reporters/20261016-thanks-a-lot-trump-wyoming-conservatives-divided-ahead-us-midterms</link><description>
Famous for its cowboy culture, Wyoming is the least populated, the most rural and the most conservative of all the US states. With two weeks to go until the midterm elections, our reporters James André and Sylvain Rousseau travelled across this Republican stronghold and found that the party of US President Donald Trump is deeply divided in the Cowboy State. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/149a27f8-c8b1-11f1-be6f-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/Reportersplus-FR.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/149a27f8-c8b1-11f1-be6f-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/Reportersplus-FR.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">848ff704-c8ac-11f1-86db-07741eb877d8</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 12:48:00 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>James ANDRE</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description>While Washington’s efforts to block Chinese electric vehicles (EVs) were originally intended to protect its domestic automotive industry, they have sparked concerns the strategy is hurting America’s carmaking competitiveness.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Fri, 16 Oct 2026 14:30:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Beyond pointing your phone at the night sky, this is how to use stargazing apps effectively ]]> Whether you are a seasoned astronomer or a newcomer to the hobby, the best stargazing apps have the potential to seriously enhance your skywatching experience. But it's easy to overlook just how useful these portable programs can be.

That's why we've put together this guide to getting the best use out of stargazing apps, from identifying stars and constellations through to seeking out dark sky sites and beyond. You will wonder how you ever managed without them.

So read on and get ready to take your stargazing to the next level. And if you're wondering how else technology can take the work out of skywatching, we've also rounded up the best smart telescopes.

Using stargazing apps

Before we explore specific uses, there are a few things you need to know about using the best stargazing apps on your Apple or Android device.

Firstly, while some apps support offline use, you'll typically need a mobile or Wi-Fi signal with data to make the most of these apps.

Also, some apps lock certain features behind a paywall. Pay for Stellarium Plus, for example, and you get an additional 2 million deep sky objects, the ability to connect to certain telescopes and more.

Finally, while many stargazing apps are relatively intuitive, we'd recommend you familiarize yourself with them at home before taking them out into the field.

Identifying stars in the field

One of the most common and convenient uses for stargazing apps is identifying stars, constellations and more, just by pointing your phone's camera at them.

It really is that simple. Take Sky Tonight, which we think is the best stargazing app for AR (augmented reality). Launch the app, grant it camera access and turn it towards the object you want to identify. The name will appear on screen and you can also tap to learn more about it, whether it's a star, constellation, planet or nebula.

Conversely, you can also use the app to find specific objects in the sky. Want to view Uranus at opposition this Nov. 25 but aren't sure where to look? Search for it in Sky Tonight and the app will point you to it.

Identifiying stars from photographs

Being able to identify night sky objects in the field is a real boon, but what if you've already taken a photograph and want to identify which stars were visible?

That's where apps like Sky Walk 2 come in. If possible, you should return to the location where the photograph was taken, but if that's not possible, you can input GPS co-ordinates and Sky Walk 2 will show you the view from that location.

Next, using the clock icon and slider, alter the date to the exact time you took the photograph (or as near as possible). You will then be shown the night sky as it was at the time. You can now tap on the star or stars you want to identify and Sky Walk 2 will tell you the name.

Sky Walk 2 isn't the only app to offer such a facility, but in Sky Walk 2's case this feature is present in the free version of the app.

Finding dark sky sites

It's a sad fact that light pollution has made it harder for astronomers to study the night sky. While the planets in our solar system are still visible, sky glow obscures more distant objects, such as fainter stars.

You could travel to a dark sky reserve but, with the aid of one of several stargazing apps, it is also possible to find dark sky sites closer to home.

Apps like Sky Safari and the simply named Light Pollution Map will show you the light pollution levels locally and globally, estimated on the Bortle scale. The latter app colors the map, with pink the most light pollution and black the least.

In just a few seconds you can find out how light polluted your local area is, and use the map to find a location nearby where the sky is dark, or at least darker.

Planning a stargazing trip

Are you planning a stargazing trip? Then you'll be happy to hear there's an app for that. There are several, in fact, but Sky Safari has all you need to plan your next outing. You can create observation lists, find out when and where objects are visible, and while it won't book your tickets for you, it comes close.

Our reviewer Jamie Carter used the app to plan his observations of conjunctions, specific moon views and astrophotography opportunities. Coupled with its light pollution map, it will be a huge help in putting together an itinerary for your skywatching trip.

Troubleshooting stargazing apps

Hopefully you'll have a smooth experience, but if you're having issues, here are a few things to try.

  • Take your phone out of its case. Magnetic clasps can interfere with internal sensors.
  • Make sure location services are enabled. Many apps use GPS to show you the correct view.
  • Check your phone's clock. If your clock is not set accurately, apps may display an incorrect sky
  • Swoop your phone in a figure eight motion. This can help calibrate your phone's "compass".
  • Make sure you have a signal, and that data is enabled. Unless the app has an offline mode you will still need a connection. Signal may be poor at dark sky sites.
  • Check each app's permissions. Location aside, Augmented Reality (AR) stargazing apps will need camera access.
  • We've got you covered with reviews and rankings of the best telescopes, binoculars, star projectors, cameras, drones, Lego, streaming and more.

]]> <![CDATA[ Supermassive black hole blasts out a neon 'treble clef' | Space photo of the day for Oct. 16, 2026 ]]>

What looks like a neon pink treble clef floating out in space is actually a bizarre source of radio waves spotted deep in the cosmos.

What is it?

Scientists using NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory have peered far out into space to look at strange radio waves coming from what they have nicknamed the "treble clef" because of its distinct shape, which looks a lot like the musical notation.

Using Chandra, as well as the German Extended RÖntgen Survey with an Imaging Telescope Array (eROSITA) X-ray telescope, researchers looking at this strange sight spotted a big cloud of blue gas, which we can see in this image, along with radio signals (seen here in bright pink). They think that this object is actually a huge galaxy cluster made up of two different clusters that are in the process of merging.

Why is it incredible?

The researchers think they may have gotten to the bottom of where these radio waves are coming from, they report in a new study.

The team thinks that the treble clef-shaped radio signals were created by an outburst from a supermassive black hole. They believe that this outburst pushed clouds of charged particles and magnetic fields away from the galaxy cluster's center, producing bright radio waves.

According to the scientists, following this bright outburst, there was likely an extreme collision between two galaxy clusters. This cosmic smash-up either compressed or somehow reenergized these charged particles to amplify the radio signal.

When we see beautiful images of objects in space such as this, they can seem just like peaceful, colorful, cosmic clouds. But when you look a bit deeper, these spectacular scenes can actually be evidence of violent, chaotic events.

This work was described in a study published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

It directs federal agencies to replace any mention of "artificial intelligence" and "AI" with "super intelligence" and "SI" in all official government communications. The White House argues that AI has advanced beyond simple automation or imitations of human intelligence, and that language befitting "a new era of Super Intelligence" is needed to better reflect the technology's emerging capabilities.

Despite introducing the new name, the order retains the federal government's existing definition of artificial intelligence, which broadly covers machine-based learning systems capable of making predictions, recommendations or decisions. That means technologies already classified as AI can now be designated "super intelligence" without demonstrating any additional capabilities.

To follow suit, NASA's Office of Communications (OCOMM) and Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) distributed an internal implementation schedule that outlines the span of work that the agency's multiple comms teams now have ahead of them.

"Effective immediately, we must use "super intelligence" and "SI" in all in-scope content/publications," the document says, bolding the key terms.

It covers both internal and external communications and instructs NASA employees to use "super intelligence" and "SI" in all new "presentations, exhibits, printed materials, media interviews, or other collateral or content for external audiences."

Internally, the policy applies to all official employee communications, NASA style guides, intra-agency websites and IT systems referenced in public-facing communications or official materials. And NASA's instructions echo Trump's directive forgoing any kind of transitional language.

"NASA is … adopting the terminology ‘Super Intelligence’ as the agency continues to expand the use of these rapidly advancing technologies across its missions," agency officials told Space.com in an emailed statement. "NASA is already applying SI to advance mission planning, autonomous systems, scientific research, and the analysis of complex datasets."

Orders from the top

Agency leadership has generally been aligned with the current administration's agenda, adjusting NASA's priorities to meet the president's goals when needed. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has helped lead that charge since his appointment to the position in December 2025; he has been a champion of Trump's human spaceflight-heavy vision for the agency since his first day. That should come as no surprise; NASA is, after all, part of the executive branch, and the agency is obliged to abide by executive orders.

But Isaacman's relationship with Trump is, perhaps, more visible than that of past NASA chiefs. The duo have shared several jovial public interactions, including an unexpected phone call from Trump during a press conference celebrating the launch of NASA's Roman Space Telescope on Aug. 30. One month later, Isaacman attended a White House luncheon with more than a dozen AI tech executives, on the same day that Trump signed his super intelligence EO.

While he's not an AI company executive, Isaacman is a member of the tech-billionaire community. Before beginning his tenure at NASA, Isaacman founded and served as CEO for Shift4 Payments, a payment processing company. He used some of that fortune to charter a pair of private astronaut launches with SpaceX — Inspiration4 and Polaris Dawn, which were the first-ever all-civilian orbital spaceflight and the flight that featured the first-ever private spacewalk, respectively.

"I was honored to have an opportunity to join that luncheon," Isaacman said when asked his opinion of AI during a post-launch press conference for the SpaceX Crew-13 astronaut mission on Oct. 1. By that point, he had already added the SI nomenclature to his lexicon. "I made clear when it was my turn to speak … I am the space guy here [not an 'AI' guy]," he added as a caveat, before saying that the "potential super intelligence has … [can] change the course of civilizations."

Isaacman's embrace of the new lingo may be partially behind NASA's own accelerated efforts to bring the agency's comms in line with the administration's. One NASA employee told Space.com, "We are getting a lot of pressure from the administrator himself to act on this."

Beyond just substituting one term for the other, NASA personnel have been told not to acknowledge the previous nomenclature at all, including short-term phrases such as "SI, also/formerly known as AI."

The changes extend to related terms such as "generative AI" becoming "generative SI," with NASA's guidance directing agency messaging away from "automation." They'll now put an emphasis on how today's technologies "amplify human ingenuity and unlock new forms of creativity," the NASA document says, quoting Trump's order.

The use of the term "SI," and the direction not to use "AI," applies across all NASA's centers and mission directorates, including contractors and personnel at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, which is run by Caltech.

Specific technical citations, like "machine learning," "large language models" and "chatbot," remain acceptable, but the new terminology may run the risk of carrying different meanings in different contexts.

Technical exceptions aside, some at NASA responsible for implementing the changes think it may present more obstacles than expected. "There's concern that there's going to be a lot of confusion in the scientific community and in the general population," a NASA employee knowledgeable of the plan told Space.com, under the condition of anonymity.

In recordings of an internal NASA communications meeting obtained by Space.com, employees echoed the same concerns to their direct management and voiced some frustration over their inability to relay to the public that the changes are being made in the first place.

"We're not even supposed to use AI as a term ... it's being talked about like Voldemort or Macbeth, with people calling it 'the technology that must not be named,'" the NASA employee said.

"Super intelligence and artificial intelligence — they have two different meanings. They both are already separate things," one meeting participant said. "As a science communicator … I feel like it's our responsibility to raise our hand and say, 'Hey, this is going to confuse people. This doesn't make sense.'"

To Isaacman's credit, those worries may have a chance of being heard by him and NASA's top brass, thanks to a management culture that seems to encourage concerns at any level being brought up the ladder without reprisal.

One meeting leader references "the idea box," an anonymous online system that allows employees to submit feedback directly to agency leadership, and reminded participants that "using the tools that we have at our disposal to make those concerns heard at the top level will not hurt."

In contrast, during the transition at the start of Trump's second term last year, before Isaacman was appointed to NASA's top seat, things at some NASA centers did not always feel as open when it came to voicing concerns to management. At the time, NASA was operating under interim leadership, first by former Kennedy Space Center Director Janet Petro, from January to July 2025, then by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy from July to December.

In a statement to Space.com, NASA officials said the agency "is taking a coordinated approach to incorporating this direction across agency communications and digital resources while maintaining the functionality and accessibility of its systems and services."

"The agency will continue to communicate its research, findings, and technological advancements accurately and transparently,” the statement said.

NASA already ahead of the game

While artificial intelligence encompasses a broad range of technologies, super intelligence has traditionally referred to a far more advanced, and often hypothetical (and sometimes sci-fi-level), capability that surpasses the limits of human cognition.

Beyond NASA, AI has entered into the space industry's ongoing realm of conversation in recent years, with several companies exploring the possibility of data centers in low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX is already operating the world's largest satellite network — there are currently more than 11,000 of the company's Starlink satellites in LEO, providing internet connectivity around the globe — and has proposed a constellation of up to 1 million satellites functioning as "orbital compute" for CEO Elon Musk's AI endeavors.

NASA began integrating AI into a number of its missions, both current and upcoming, well before conversations about SI stepped into the picture. One of the first to try on that hat was the agency's Perseverance rover on Mars, which used machine learning to plan and complete its first drive on the Red Planet using routes mapped out by generative AI in December 2025.

NASA has also put AI to work analyzing massive amounts of data. Surya, an AI-powered foundation model introduced by NASA and IBM last year, was trained on nine years of NASA heliophysics data to help improve space weather and solar activity forecasting. A more recent lunar collaboration between NASA and IBM was introduced last month to help researchers investigate the surface of the moon for potential deposits of water ice, and AI is central to NASA's plan for processing the massive amounts of data expected once Roman is operational.

"Foundation models" like Surya fall under the acceptable precise-language usage that NASA still considers best practice when communicating with scientific audiences, according to the agency's internal guidance. However, separate instructions for scientific publications and research documents are still being developed internally, leaving some uncertainty over how NASA researchers will reconcile the new terminology with established language used by universities, international space agencies and other scientific institutions that may not adhere to Trump's EO.

According to the agency's internal plan, a determination for scientific publications and research documents will be issued by NASA's Scientific and Technical Information, Science Mission Directorate and Chief Science Data Officer teams, along with separate guidance for official agency policy documents, both of which are listed on a page titled "Forthcoming Guidance."

Implementation

Retroactively, certain already published web pages, including applicable evergreen content in active use, will be marked for update or given an added disclaimer with an archival notice. Titles, descriptions and other metadata for older videos and podcasts may also be revised to reflect the new terminology, while the original recordings, transcripts and captions will remain unchanged. NASA's page for Perseverance's AI-guided trek across Mars' surface, for instance, is now titled, "Mapping Perseverance’s Route With SI," but "AI" is still present in the page's URL — for the time being, at least.

Soon, that URL will redirect to a new one, with "SI" in its place. NASA's internal plan divides its implementation into four phases, with proposed deadlines stretching from Oct. 9 through Dec. 23.

"Every agency is doing it at their own pace," one NASA employee told Space.com. "You'll see some places have not implemented the change yet, and others, like NASA, are pushing it forward sooner rather than later."

Phase One, which went into effect Oct. 9, included NASA's primary AI-related websites and agency personnel titles, such as that of Kevin Murphy. He is now "acting chief data and super intelligence officer," not "acting chief data and artificial intelligence officer."

Phase Two will expand the overhaul to heavily visited pages on nasa.gov and science.nasa.gov, and rename the website for JPL's Artificial Intelligence Group, ai.jpl.nasa.gov, to redirect visitors to an address reflecting the new SI terminology. The second phase's completion was initially set for implementation by Oct. 30. Sources familiar with the agency's progress, however, said that timeline was accelerated and the changes made ready to go live starting today (Oct. 16), two weeks ahead of schedule, according to a NASA employee.

Phase Three is marked for implementation by Nov. 30. It includes additional high-traffic NASA websites and the renaming of its URL for Ask Sage, a generative AI platform used by federal agencies. NASA's internal plan describes the change as a "breaking change for APIs and other integrations," meaning existing software connections may need to be updated.

According to NASA officials, "any necessary technical changes will be evaluated and implemented through established agency processes."

Finally, Phase Four, targeted for Dec. 23, will scoop up NASA's remaining, lower-traffic websites, as well as internal IT systems and tools. NASA's guidance notes that Trump's EO doesn't designate a deadline for affected agencies, and that, without accompanying direction from the Office of Personnel Management, its framework ultimately represents the authors' recommendations "in light of competing OMB (Office of Management and Budget) and agency leadership priorities."

Editors note: This story was updated at 10:10 a.m. EDT (1410 GMT) on Oct. 16 to include Statments from NASA sent after publication.

]]> <![CDATA[ Rocket Lab pushes 1st launch of next-gen Neutron rocket to 2027 ]]> We'll have to wait a bit longer to see Rocket Lab's next-gen launcher fly.

The California-based company just announced that it's pushing the debut of its powerful, partially reusable Neutron rocket from late 2026 into 2027 due to a manufacturing issue.

"We believe Neutron is going to be a game-changer, and taking the time now to solve these challenges means we're in a better position to deliver a rocket that's ready to meet the needs for the industry for years to come," Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said in a video the company posted on YouTube late on Tuesday (Oct. 13).

Beck explained the issue in depth in that seven-minute video. It concerns the cabon-fiber propellant domes in Neutron's first stage — the large caps for the vehicle's fuel tanks, which hold liquid oxygen and liquid methane.

Rocket Lab makes the domes using an automated fiber placement machine, "which lays down the carbon with speed and accuracy," Beck said.

The company noticed a problem, however, after curing a recently manufactured forward (front-facing) dome: Inspectors found some voids within the carbon-fiber layers.

The voids "don't necessarily mean that the dome would fail in flight, but our practice is to proceed only when we believe the system has the appropriate margins," Beck said. "Possible success isn't our standard."

After analysis and testing, Rocket Lab added some "mitigations" to the dome-manufacturing process — a tweak that has done the trick, according to Beck.

"We've since run another carbon composite section called the aft dome through this new process, and I'm pleased to report that it has resulted in the highest quality carbon composite dome to date, and we've solved the problem," he said.

Rocket Lab still needs to build a new forward dome, then cure and inspect it — steps that are expected to be complete by the end of the year, according to Beck. The company then needs to incorporate that hardware into a complete Neutron first stage, and then subject that stage to a battery of tests. If all goes to plan, that will all be done during the first quarter of 2027.

"From there, we expect to be in good shape to share a new target launch date," Beck said.

The newly announced delay is the latest setback for Neutron, which Rocket Lab announced in 2021. Back then, the company — which also flies the workhorse Electron small-satellite launcher — targeted a 2024 debut for the 141-foot-tall (42 meters) Neutron, which features a reusable first stage.

That timeline has been pushed back multiple times — to 2025, then to early 2026 and then, after a fuel tank ruptured during a pressure test, to late 2026.

Rocket Lab has been been steadfast throughout, stressing that it will not rush the development of a vehicle that it sees as vital to its future success.

"There's significant demand for what Neutron has to offer, including some new contracts we'll be able to talk about soon," Beck said in the video. "Those customers understand that a reliable rocket is far more valuable than an early one, and we're grateful for their trust."

]]> <![CDATA[ It's time to reassess the size of our solar system, scientists say ]]> Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system by presenting a theory which states that measurements of the Milky Way's gravitational field, including its dark matter, redraws the sun's frontier.

That theory was put forward by Jim Green, former NASA chief scientist and past director of the space agency's Planetary Science Division, along with Ed Belbruno, a professor of mathematics at Yeshiva University and a senior research associate at Princeton University.

The solar system's gravitational frontier extends to nearly 3.8 light-years from the sun, they contend, roughly 241,000 astronomical units (AU), a distance that brings the "edge" of the solar system to within the same scale as the separation between neighboring stars. ]]> <![CDATA[ Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween ]]> How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death  — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie.

That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals.

For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white, and the hottest stars glow pale blue. This is akin to a blacksmith's iron glowing red, then orange, then white-hot as it heats up. Researchers have always assumed that white dwarfs follow the same rule. However, new research suggests that these stellar corpses could glow in a range of colors including green, pink, cyan, yellow, and purple. That means the universe is far more colorful than we suspected.

"Most stars, including most white dwarfs, behave like 'perfect radiators,' so their color is set almost entirely by temperature. But nobody had really looked into what else might be possible for white dwarfs," team leader Mark Hollands of the University of Warwick said in a statement sent to Space.com.

"It turns out these incredibly dense stars caaaaan produce colors nobody expected, and some of them genuinely surprised me."

How white dwarfs break stellar color rules

White dwarfs get their name because when they were discovered, they appeared surprisingly hot and glowed white or pale blue. However, this new research suggests that this slightly bland and uniform appearance is because no white dwarf is close enough for Earthbound astronomers to see their true colors.

The key to the rainbow-like array of colors this team suggests white dwarfs could possess is their density. White dwarfs form when stars with a mass roughly that of the sun run out of fuel and can no longer support themselves against their own gravity, causing their cores to collapse. As a result, the matter that makes up white dwarfs is around the density of water, millions of times denser than the sun's surface, the photosphere.

In these conditions, elements like carbon, calcium, and sodium can interact with the surrounding dense helium plasma and absorb light across a wider range of colors than they would at lower densities. That shifts the colors of white dwarfs away from the white/light blue seen for a perfect radiator of heat.

The researchers found that the colors of white dwarfs would fit into distinct groups tied to the individual chemical makeup of the stellar remnant's atmosphere.

White dwarfs abundant in carbon should be pink or purple, while those that have been enriched with debris from consumed asteroids and comets, and the remains of old planetary systems, would take a more yellow hue. Cooler white dwarfs with mixed hydrogen and helium atmospheres often would glow cyan or pale blue, caused as hydrogen molecules collide with helium atoms in their dense atmospheres.

One of the most striking examples of white dwarf coloration, however, would arise when one of these living dead stars starts feeding on the planets around it like a horror movie zombie.

Zombie white dwarfs go green

The researchers found that some dead star white dwarfs can go a little green around the gills after snacking on orbiting planets.

An example of this is WD J1330+6435, a cool white dwarf located around 326 light-years away, which has been accreting rocky material from a planetary companion. This has enriched its atmosphere with calcium, lithium, and sodium, and the team's model suggests this would have led WD J1330+6435 to adopt a green hue.

But unlike the green-tinged zombies of George Romero's classic Dawn of the Dead, there are no hordes of these green-faced cosmic zombies ... yet.

The researchers think that no other star, living or dead, has ever been credibly reported as green. That makes WD J1330+6435 the first known genuinely green star.

"The traces of sodium in the atmosphere of this white dwarf absorb the orange part of the spectrum, leaving behind a ghostly green glow," Hollands said. "Imagine standing on a planet and looking up at a green star. It feels like something out of science fiction."

Scientists see red

The team didn't just discover that a known white dwarf is the first-ever green star; they also discovered what could be the reddest star ever in the form of the white dwarf WD J1011+2845.

Located just 48 light-years from Earth, this white dwarf has a deep convection zone that carries carbon from its core to its surface. These carbon molecules distort light from the white dwarf, causing a deep salmon-pink glow unlike anything seen in any other star.

Despite this rainbow of white dwarfs, the team theorizes that white is still the most common color for these stellar corpses. Only five of the 151 white dwarfs within around 65 light-years of Earth have extraordinary coloring. Extrapolating this to the total population of white dwarfs, the team estimates that only one in 30 of these dead stars has an unusual color.

"One in thirty might not sound like a huge fraction, but across the entire population of white dwarfs in the universe, that is still a lot of oddly colored stars out there," Boris Gänsicke, Department of Physics, University of Warwick, said. "Yet if we take the median across a representative population of white dwarfs, we found that the average white dwarf really is white."

The team's research was published on Thursday (Oct. 14) in the journal RAS Techniques and Instruments.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn ]]>

On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida.

It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn, with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005.

Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017.

Running low on fuel, NASA chose to steer Cassini straight into Saturn's atmosphere, where the spacecraft was destroyed.

Why it mattered

NASA's Cassini mission to Saturn (which carried the European Space Agency's Huygens lander to Titan) was a flagship planetary mission like no other ever when it first launched toward the ringed planet.

The $3.26 billion Cassini spacecraft became the first probe ever to orbit Saturn when it arrived in 2004. It revealed Saturn's rings as active and dynamic structures, as intricate and complex as they are beautiful to observe.

And it delivered Huygens to Titan, then followed up with a series of Titan flybys that revealed the cloudy moon could have liquid hydrocarbon rain, rivers, lakes and seas.

Perhaps the most exciting discoveries were the most surprising.

Cassini discovered a strange hexagon-shaped jetstream encircling Saturn's north pole and revealed massive hurricane-like vortexes over both of the planet's poles. In 2010, Cassini watched as a giant storm formed in Saturn's northern hemisphere, then grew to encircle the entire planet through 2011.

The spacecraft also discovered icy plumes of water erupting from Saturn's moon Enceladus, revealing new clues into that moon's subsurface ocean of liquid water, complete with hydrothermal events like those found in Earth's oceans.

It was to protect Enceladus, Titan and other Saturn moons that NASA ultimated sent Cassini into a death dive into Saturn at the end of its mission. The space agency wanted to prevent any chance of contamination at those pristine moons.

"NASA’s Cassini spacecraft and ESA’s Huygens probe expanded our understanding of the kinds of worlds where life might exist and eight more reasons the mission changed the course of planetary exploration," NASA said in an overview.

SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Oct. 15).

A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today at 8:01 p.m. EDT (5:01 p.m. local time; 0001 GMT on Oct. 16), rising into clear blue skies above the Golden State's central coast.

Such visibly striking launches are far from guaranteed; Vandenberg and its scenic surroundings are often blanketed by fog, making rocket watching in the area a dicey proposition.

This evening's launch kicked off the USSF-481 mission, which is delivering mysterious payloads to an undisclosed location in the final frontier.

SpaceX didn't provide much more info during its launch webcast; it ended just after the Falcon 9 first stage's landing, which occurred as planned about 8.5 minutes after launch on the drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

USSF-481 was the 28th flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1081. Sixteen of its previous 27 launches were devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink broadband megaconstellation in low Earth orbit, according to a SpaceX mission description.

Previous Booster 1081 missions

Crew-7 | CRS-29 | PACE | Transporter-10 | EarthCARE | NROL-186 | Transporter-13 | TRACERS | NROL-48 | COSMO-SkyMed Second Generation FM3 | 16 Starlink missions

USSF-481 was the 114th Falcon 9 mission of the year. The vast majority of the rocket's flights in 2026 — more than 70% of them — have been Starlink missions.

SpaceX has also launched its Falcon Heavy and Starship rockets three times so far this year. Falcon Heavy is an operational vehicle, but the fully reusable Starship remains in the test-flight phase. It reached orbit for the first time on its most recent launch, which occurred on Sept. 28.

Editor's note: This story was updated at 8:30 p.m. ET on Oct. 15 with news of successful launch and rocket landing.

The world of smart technology in stargazing optics is constantly pushing forward but it tends to move in waves in terms of actual "new" technology. Obviously, smart telescopes improve as new releases come out, usually with higher resolution and an upgraded optical design, but they are still just improvements on a base model. For years, Vaonis has improved and developed their Vespera models, but the announcement of the Atlas reveals a potential new direction for the company.

The Atlas system is the first-ever modular smart telescope system for Vaonis, with a base dock system fitted with two ports for connecting two imaging modules (an optical tube with a sensor). The Atlas 80 imaging module is an optical tube with a 3.15-in (80 mm) aperture and a Sony IMX585 8.3MP sensor, designed for imaging deep-space objects such as galaxies, nebulas and star clusters. Attaching identical imaging modules allows you to image targets quicker and with more detail, but the most intriguing part of this whole release is not actually available yet.

Vaonis has promised to expand the Atlas ecosystem after launch, including a backpack, filters, an equatorial wedge and most importantly, new imaging modules. The next planned imaging module is for planetary observation, which could be a game changer. If you have used a smart telescope for planetary observation, you will know that they produce grainy blobs when compared to their stunning deep space imagery. Vaonis might not just be introducing modularity for smart telescopes; they might also be introducing the ability to get a good photo of a planet with one.

Atlas pre-orders open today and are available from BH Photo and Video and Adorama. The special preorder pricing is available until Nov. 15, with the First shipments expected in March 2027. This release includes the SkyDock along with either one Atlas 80 or two Atlas 80 imaging modules.

Key features: Modular design, Atlas 80 imaging module with 3.15-in (80 mm) apochromatic quadruplet lens, 360 mm focal length, f/4.5 focal ratio and a Sony IMX585 8.3-megapixel sensor, app-controlled, automatic pointing and imaging (Go-To function), 16.1-in (41 cm) height when closed (excluding tripod), 14.3 lb (6.5 kg) weight, up to 6 hours of battery life.

Product launched: Oct 2026

Price comparison for Vaonis Atlas with single optical tube: B&H PhotoVideo: Likely starting at $3,990 | Adorama: Starting at $3,990

✅ Buy it if: You want to invest in a smart telescope but are interested in getting the best photographs of a wide range of night sky targets, including deep-space objects and planets.

❌ Don't buy it if: You don't care about interchangeability or adaptability from your smart telescope and are mainly interested in using it to photograph deep-sky objects.

Slated for launch in 2028, SR-1 Freedom is the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft and is assigned the duty of dropping off the SkyFall entry capsule loaded with the trio of aerial vehicles at the Red Planet. SR-1's trajectory will deliver the SkyFall helicopters in Mars' northern hemisphere during the planet's spring season to avoid dust storms.

SkyFall is based on the success of the first aerial craft to float about the Red Planet, Ingenuity, which flew over 70 missions at Jezero Crater before it finally broke a rotor. It was designed to fly five. The SkyFall mission will consist of three identical helicopters to be deployed by an entry vehicle in the atmosphere, let loose at roughly under a mile (3,300 feet or 1,000 meters) above Mars, with each of the craft landing independently.

Regions of interest

The SkyFall mission is to conduct investigations that address objectives relevant for science and preparing for human exploration of Mars. Anticipated flights of the vehicles will travel outside of the landing ellipse to regions of interest within a broader exploration zone.

However, there are further science-focused flight paths and regions that have yet to be determined. NASA intends for the SkyFall helicopters to go to multiple regions of scientific interest on Mars.

NASA's Mars Exploration Program, along with the SkyFall project at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), will work together to pick those "why and where" paths to navigate.

A first workshop on potential landing sites for the SkyFall mission and adjacent exploration zones of high scientific value is slated for early next year. And as always, sites and zones on Mars for the choppers means satisfying engineering constraints imposed by the project and spacecraft design.

Given the rapid development cadence of the SkyFall mission, decisions are to be fast-paced, but are geared to maximizing science value of the endeavor.

What Mars researchers are after will be a ranked list of potential landing sites that will be studied in more detail by the SkyFall project and science community, prior to a second workshop to be held in late 2027.

Notional flight trajectories

On the table are potential science value and notional flight trajectories of individual landing sites given the capabilities and payload of the SkyFall helicopters.

Landing site selection will occur after the back-to-back landing site workshops next year, said Matthew Golombek, SkyFall Project Scientist at JPL.

"The project has identified a design reference landing site that targets subsurface water ice deposits with glacial/periglacial terrains," Golombek told Space.com.

Given their deployment, how much real estate will the aerial vessel assault study?

Golombek said that the helicopters are capable of flying one to two kilometers every other sol, so flight traverses of 125 miles to a little over 185 miles (200-300 kilometers) are possible.

"The helicopters are designed to last 6 months, with a goal of one Earth year and each can fly every other sol so multiple flights are expected," Golombek added.

Thanks to the success of the Perseverance rover's unleashing of the Ingenuity rotorcraft, Golombek said that there are a host of lessons learned, as well as engineering additions to be made to the set of SkyFall vehicles.

Nominal payload

"Although the helicopters are slightly larger than Ingenuity, they are being designed to operate in exactly the same way, so all of the experience with Ingenuity operations will be directly relevant," said Golombek.

The nominal payload to be toted around the Red Planet will be identical for all three helicopters, consisting of five instruments, plus engineering navigation cameras. Those instruments are to investigate the subsurface structure of Mars, the geomorphology and geology of surface terrains, as well as look at the meteorology of the atmosphere and the radiation environment.

Although there is no dedicated hardware to directly measure winds, the helicopters themselves can serve as on-the-spot wind sensors, even shifting to "Balloon Mode," whereby a helicopter will drift in the background wind.

Radar love

Each low-flying helicopter is outfitted with a ground penetrating radar (GPR) instrument, one that can detect layering in the near surface, at depths unobservable by orbital radar.

Those layers could be assembled from rocky material, buried ice, or combinations of the two. Detection of near-surface ice is of interest both scientifically as well as in support of future human expeditions to Mars.

Subsurface ice not only preserves a record of past Martian climate but also serves as a "high-priority environment" that might have served as a habitat of past…or Martian life resident today.

SkyFall maneuver

AeroVironment of Arlington, Virginia is partnering with JPL, selected last August to co-design and co-manufacture the SkyFall helicopters. They too are building on their experience as co‑developers of NASA's Ingenuity Mars helicopter that made those 72 flights at Jezero Crater on Mars.

"Now, with SkyFall, we're taking AV's high‑volume uncrewed systems mindset into planetary exploration and showing that Mars helicopters can be built as a repeatable product line, not a one‑off delivery," said Jeff Rodrian, Head of MacCready Works, AV's advanced research and development organization.

A special "SkyFall maneuver" is to be utilized in deploying the three aerial craft. They will be released directly from the carrier spacecraft into the Martian atmosphere, where they separate, deploy, descend, and land under their own power.

"By eliminating the need for a single-use lander stage or a host rover (as Ingenuity required with Perseverance), this approach significantly reduces the technical and financial risk of getting to the Martian surface," explains an AeroVironment statement.

Mountains of data

"Just like here on Earth, Mars helicopters can cover distance quickly and can go places that might be impossible to reach by ground," said Will Pomerantz, Head of Space Ventures at AeroVironment.

The science community may guide these helicopters to locations, Pomerantz said, where the ground penetrating radar can map out the specific spots of ice below the martian surface.

"The three SkyFall helicopters are going to show us parts of Mars we've never seen before and return mountains of data for scientists to pore over," said Pomerantz.

  <item>
   <title>Ewa Farna zaskočila hráče Zrádců. Miluju tě, vyhrkl jeden ze soutěžících</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/kultura/zradci-ewa-farna/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=kultura</link>
   <description>Překvapení, jaké Zrádci nejspíš nezažili. Do pátého dílu detektivní show na Primě nečekaně vstoupili Ewa Farna a Mirai. Šel z nich skutečný strach - vypadali totiž jako příchozí ze záhrobí. Proměna byla dokonalá.</description>

    <media:description>Ewa Farna zaskočila hráče televizních Zrádců. V temném nalíčení a ve sklepení Křivoklátu působila jako duch.</media:description>

  <item>
   <title>Hrůza v obci na Plzeňsku: Propuštěný vrah znásilnil a uškrtil vlastní matku</title>
   <link>https://plzensky.denik.cz/krimi/vrah-herbrych-matka-znasilneni-dozivoti-pribehy-zla-plzensko/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=krimi</link>
   <description>Vladimír Herbrych ze Sokolovska byl ve vážných problémech už od mládí. Když mu bylo 32 let, zabil v Praze 83letou Žofii D. Po propuštění z vězení mu poskytla azyl jeho matka Žofie S., která ho nechala bydlet u sebe v Sedlci u Starého Plzence na Plzeňsku. Odvděčil se jí tím, že ji po hádce také zavraždil. A znásilnil a okradl. Příběh dvojnásobného vraha Herbrycha, který byl odsouzen na doživotí, je dalším pokračováním seriálu Deníku Příběhy zla.</description>
   <pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://plzensky.denik.cz/krimi/vrah-herbrych-matka-znasilneni-dozivoti-pribehy-zla-plzensko/</guid>
   <category>Krimi</category>
   <enclosure url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/cff/cfff7fcf-5401-420c-a650-55250bd25eb2.jpeg" length="0" type="image/jpeg"/>
   <media:content url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/cff/cfff7fcf-5401-420c-a650-55250bd25eb2.jpeg" medium="image" height="768" width="1366">
    <media:description>Dům v Sedlci, kde Hebrych zavraždil svoji matku. Dnes už tu žijí lidé, kteří s tragédií nemají nic společného.</media:description>
    <media:credit>Petr Eret</media:credit>
   </media:content>
  </item>

   <title>Pavel se vrátil z dovolené v Maroku. Opět zvažoval tryskáč, zvolil ale linku</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/prezident-petr-pavel-maroko-dovolena-navrat/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Prezident republiky Petr Pavel se ve čtvrtek večer vrátil z dovolené v Maroku. Do Prahy přiletěl běžnou nízkonákladovou linkou, uvedl server iDnes.cz. Do Česka se na několik hodin vrátil už před týdnem, aby odevzdal hlas v komunálních volbách, tehdy ale využil soukromý marocký tryskáč.</description>

      <title>Rozbitá okna a semafory, ministerstvo v ohni. Albánií zmítají studentské protesty</title>

      <description>Tisíce mladých lidí při pokračujících násilných studentských protestech pochodovaly albánskou metropolí. Rozbíjeli při tom okna a semafory.       <description>V části Česka se dnes ve dvě hodiny odpoledne opět otevřely volební místnosti. Lidé si zvolí celkem 22 senátorů. Zástupci hnutí STAN mohou po šesti letech zopakovat své vítězství. <description>Jednotné měsíční hlá&#353;ení zaměstnavatele (JMHZ) má státu umožnit sbírat dal&#353;í údaje o zaměstnancích a zpřístupnit je více úřadům. Ministerstvo práce a sociálních věcí navrhuje změny, které mají reagovat na novou legislativu i praktické potřeby státních institucí. K návrhu přibyly nové dokumenty v oficiálním systému ODok.</description>

<description>Český národní polovodičový klastr ve spolupráci s Českým polovodičovým centrem vytvořily užitečný online nástroj. Jde o katalog takzvaných IP bloků používaných při vývoji čipů. <link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/miliarda-jim-trvala-tri-roky-druha-jen-pet-mesicu-ceskou-ai-nadeji-uz-pouzivaji-meta-xiaomi-nebo-nvidia/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český startup E2B aktuálně patří k největ&#353;ím technologickým nadějím země. Pro AI agenty umožňuje velice rychle spou&#353;tět sandboxy, tedy izolovaná prostředí, v nichž agenti mohou běžet, vykonat práci a sandbox následně ukončit. E2B pokračuje v silném růstu. Firma informovala, že jí trvalo tři roky, než u ní zákazníci rozjeli miliardu sandboxů. Teď pokočila metu dvou miliard sandboxů s tím, že druhá miliarda trvala pouze pět měsíců.</description>

 <title>Je lepší se ničím nechlubit. Když se něco podaří opravit, zaútočí další drony, říká obyvatelka Kyjeva</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/je-lepsi-se-nicim-nechlubit-kdyz-se-neco-podari-opravit-zautoci-dalsi-drony-rika_2610161329_med</link>
 <description>Rusko dále pokračuje v intenzivních útocích na Kyjev. „Snažíme se žít normálně, ale je to iluze. Od konce srpna jsou slyšet výbuchy prakticky každou hodinu a k tomu se přidala nová taktika balistických útoků. Lidé ztrácejí možnost včas se ukrýt a ve městě jsou každý den civilní oběti,“ popisuje právnička Katja Andrejevová žijící v Kyjevě.</description>

<item>
 <title>Kdo prosazuje ETS2, prohraje volby, vzkázal Babiš na summitu. V4 žádá nové vyhodnocení povolenek</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/kdo-prosazuje-ets2-prohraje-volby-vzkazal-babis-na-summitu-v4-zada-nove_2610161241_kch</link>
 <description>Několika členským státům Evropské unie včetně Česka se do závěrů summitu EU podařilo dostat novou výzvu Evropské komisi, aby znovu vyhodnotila dopady systému emisních povolenek ETS2. Vyplývá to ze závěrů prvního dne jednání, který proběhl ve čtvrtek. Evropská rada rovněž nově výslovně zdůraznila, že v rámci přezkumu systému ETS je třeba omezit kolísání cen emisních povolenek a zmírnit jejich dopad na ceny elektřiny.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-16t070106z_8_261016-125829_kch.JPG?itok=2HQXgXJz" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 12:41:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>ONLINE: EU nezruší sankce vůči Rusku, dokud Moskva neukončí válku, řekla von der Leyenová</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-eu-nezrusi-sankce-vuci-rusku-dokud-moskva-neukonci-valku-rekla-von-der_2610161049_med</link>
 <description>Evropská unie nezruší žádné sankce vůči Rusku, dokud Rusko neukončí svou válku na Ukrajině, uvedla při příchodu na summit EU v Bruselu šéfka Evropské komise Ursula von der Leyenová. Ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj během společného prohlášení právě se šéfkou EK a předsedou unijních summitů Antóniem Costou poděkoval Evropské unii za podporu. Podpora Ukrajiny je jedním z hlavních témat dnešního jednání.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-06-09t000000z_1_261016-105212_med.JPG?itok=dRv6jMyv" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:49:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Dohoda o rozpočtu EU do Vánoc nebude, myslí si Babiš. Rozdíly v pozicích států jsou prý příliš velké</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/dohoda-o-rozpoctu-eu-do-vanoc-nebude-mysli-si-babis-rozdily-v-pozicich-statu_2610161024_kch</link>
 <description>Premiér Andrej Babiš (ANO) se po jednání v Bruselu domnívá, že se lídrům nepodaří dosáhnout dohody o budoucím víceletém rozpočtu EU do konce letošního roku. Stane se tak nejspíš až v únoru či v březnu. Unijní prezidenti a premiéři vedli debatu o svých požadavcích do rozpočtu ve čtvrtek odpoledne a panují mezi nimi zásadní rozdíly. Předseda Evropské rady António Costa přitom několikrát zdůraznil, že doufá v dohodu právě nejpozději v prosinci.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-07-08t110907z_1_260930-224916_jar.JPG?itok=mj_W6l5d" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Po střelbě na základní škole v Oregonu zemřeli tři žáci a vyučující. Útočníka zneškodnil kolemjdoucí</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/po-strelbe-na-zakladni-skole-v-oregonu-zemreli-tri-zaci-a-vyucujici-utocnika_2610160651_lhv</link>
 <description>Tři žáci ve věku pět, osm a jedenáct let a jeden učitel zemřeli po čtvrteční střelbě na základní škole ve městě Bend v americkém státě Oregon, informovala místní policie. Mrtvý je i šestnáctiletý střelec, kterého zastřelil jeden z místních lidí. Další dva zraněné převezly sanitky do nemocnic, uvádí americká média.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-15t230521z_1_261016-062809_lhv.JPG?itok=4QFuIrNm" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>

 <description>Postkomunistická, antikapitalistická, krajně levicová. Také radikální? A extrémní? Die Linke ovládla Berlín, zatím jen ve volbách, ale vyjednává o koalici. Jak o ní mluvit?</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Kalhousová: Izraelci berou volby jako spor o duši země. Zprávy o svých zločinech v Gaze nesou špatně</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/kalhousova-izraelci-berou-volby-jako-spor-o-dusi-zeme-zpravy-o-svych-zlocinech-v_2610160010_brz</link>
 <description>Izrael čekají první volby od začátku současné války v Pásmu Gazy, která začala po teroristickém útoku Hamásu ze 7. října 2023. O novém složení jednokomorového Knesetu rozhodnou voličky a voliči za dva týdny. „Izraelská společnost nevnímá volby pouze jako spor o politické ideje, ale o duši Izraele a o to, jaký jejich stát bude,“ říká pro Český rozhlas Plus ředitelka Herzlova centra izraelských studií na Univerzitě Karlově Irena Kalhousová.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Zmije, chřestýš nebo leguán. Celníci v Německu našli v zavazadle Mexičana 92 hadů a ještěrů</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/zmije-chrestys-nebo-leguan-celnici-v-nemecku-nasli-v-zavazadle-mexicana-92-hadu_2610152345_vsn</link>
 <description>Němečtí celníci našli v zavazadle muže cestujícího z Mexika 37 jedovatých hadů a 55 ještěrů. Muž zvířata ukrýval v plastových nádobách, lahvičkách od šamponů a krémů, ale i v ponožkách. Asi 30 zvířat během cesty nebo krátce po ní uhynulo kvůli nevyhovujícím podmínkám, informovala ve čtvrtek agentura AFP.</description>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/zemreli-protoze-na-zdravotniky-cekali-moc-dlouho-pripad-dvou-australanu_2610152235_brz</link>
 <description>Úřady ve státě Queensland na severovýchodě Austrálie začaly vyšetřovat samostatné případy dvou pacientů, kteří v uplynulém týdnu zemřeli při čekání na lékařskou péči. Informoval o tom web ABC.</description>

<item>
 <title>V eurotunelu se na francouzské straně průlivu srazil autobus s nákladním vlakem, zranilo se 19 lidí</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/v-eurotunelu-se-na-francouzske-strane-prulivu-srazil-autobus-s-nakladnim-vlakem_2610152212_brz</link>
 <description>Srážka autobusu s nákladním vlakem u vjezdu do eurotunelu na francouzské straně Lamanšského průlivu si ve čtvrtek večer vyžádala 19 zraněných. Dva lidé mají vážná zranění, ale nikdo není v ohrožení života, uvedly francouzské úřady. Provoz nákladních vlaků byl v obou směrech dočasně přerušen, osobních vlaků se událost nedotkla, informovala francouzská média. Podle francouzských médií vezl autobus stavební dělníky.</description>

České dráhy (ČD) na tento den připravily Den se železnicí na Liberecku, který nabídne nezapomenutelné zážitky pro malé i velké.</description></item><item><title>Souboj o Senát na Českolipsku. Rozhodne se mezi hejtmanem a starostkou Lípy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903179-souboj-o-senat-na-ceskolipsku-rozhodne-se-mezi-hejtmanem-a-starostkou-lipy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903179-souboj-o-senat-na-ceskolipsku-rozhodne-se-mezi-hejtmanem-a-starostkou-lipy.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 14:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Také v části Libereckého kraje se rozhodne o novém senátorovi. Volí se v okrsku 36, kam spadá Českolipsko, ale také část Liberecka a Mělnicka. Do druhého kola postoupila končící starostka České Lípy Jitka Volfová (ANO) a hejtman Libereckého kraje Martin Půta (Starostové pro LK).</description></item><item><title>VIDEO: Šokující výlet s dědečkem, v České Lípě opíjel a učil kouřit děti (5 a 12)</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903204-video-sokujici-vylet-s-dedeckem-v-ceske-lipe-opijel-a-ucil-kourit-deti-5-a-12.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903204-video-sokujici-vylet-s-dedeckem-v-ceske-lipe-opijel-a-ucil-kourit-deti-5-a-12.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 13:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Místo zmrzliny či dortu alkohol a tabák. Svéráznou představu rodinného výletu překazil v České Lípě v Hrnčířské ulici asistent prevence kriminality. Dědeček dával pít pivo a kouřit cigarety svým vnukům ve věku 5 a 12 let přímo na ulici. Případem se už zabývá správní orgán.</description></item><item><title>Křižovatka Sněhulák se opět uzavře. Letos už naposledy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903176-krizovatka-snehulak-se-opet-uzavre-letos-uz-naposledy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903176-krizovatka-snehulak-se-opet-uzavre-letos-uz-naposledy.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 12:12:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Křižovatku zvanou Sněhulák čeká během páteční noci poslední letošní uzavírka. Důvodem je oprava mostu silnice I/35 nad křižovatkou. Ta se uzavře v pátek v 18 hodin a uzavírka potrvá do sobotní osmé hodiny ráno.</description></item><item><title>Další krok k záchraně barokního dvora zámku Zákupy: Začíná obnova západní části</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/903165-dalsi-krok-k-zachrane-barokniho-dvora-zamku-zakupy-zacina-obnova-zapadni-casti.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/903165-dalsi-krok-k-zachrane-barokniho-dvora-zamku-zakupy-zacina-obnova-zapadni-casti.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Kultura</category><description>Na státním zámku Zákupy začala obnova západní části barokního hospodářského dvora za 242 milionů korun. Práce potrvají do roku 2029 a zajistí stavební záchranu objektu i prostory pro nový archeologický depozitář. Pokračující obnova je dalším krokem k záchraně tohoto unikátního komplexu.</description></item><item><title>Meteorologové prozradili, jaký bude podzim</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903155-meteorologove-prozradili-jaky-bude-podzim.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903155-meteorologove-prozradili-jaky-bude-podzim.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 08:55:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Markéta Hamerníková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Deštivého podzimu se zatím obávat nemusíme. Přestože o víkendu na severu Čech zaprší, výhled na dalších sedm až deset dní slibuje převážně suché počasí. Meteorologové očekávají méně srážek, než je pro toto období obvyklé.</description></item><item><title>Nevšední a zábavný: Orfeus v podsvětí v Liberci moderně a se sociálními sítěmi</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/903164-orfeus-v-podsveti-dostal-v-liberci-moderni-podobu-se-socialnimi-sitemi.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/903164-orfeus-v-podsveti-dostal-v-liberci-moderni-podobu-se-socialnimi-sitemi.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 06:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Kultura</category><description>Do současného jazyka se sociálními sítěmi i mobilními telefony převedlo liberecké divadlo operetu Orfeus v podsvětí od Jacquese Offenbacha. V premiéře uvede dílo o manželských radostech a strastech v sobotu. Větší akcent než v původní verzi bude mít v liberecké úpravě postava Veřejného mínění.</description></item><item><title>Dýně v neděli zaplní centrum Liberce</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903090-dyne-v-nedeli-zaplni-centrum-liberce.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903090-dyne-v-nedeli-zaplni-centrum-liberce.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 20:01:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Náměstí před libereckou radnicí promění v místo podzimní atmosféry, vůní a chutí. Od 10 do 16 hodin se zde uskuteční tradiční Dýňová neděle. Akce nabídne speciální nejen dýňový trh, kulinářskou soutěž, ochutnávky i bohatý doprovodný program pro děti i dospělé. Vstup je zdarma.</description></item><item><title>V Kauflandu v Jablonci našli inspektoři výživu dřív stahovanou z prodeje kvůli toxinu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903149-v-kauflandu-v-jablonci-nasli-inspektori-vyzivu-driv-stahovanou-z-prodeje-kvuli-toxinu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903149-v-kauflandu-v-jablonci-nasli-inspektori-vyzivu-driv-stahovanou-z-prodeje-kvuli-toxinu.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 18:53:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Kojenecké výživy značky Nutrilon, dříve stahované z prodeje kvůli podezření na výskyt toxinu cereulid, se opětovně objevily v některých prodejnách Kauflandu, například v Jablonci nad Nisou. Státní zemědělská a potravinářská inspekce (SZPI) to zjistila při cílené kontrole tří prodejen společnosti.</description></item><item><title>Víte, zda vaše dítě sedí v autě skutečně bezpečně? Přijďte to zjistit do OC NISA</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902951-vite-zda-vase-dite-sedi-v-aute-skutecne-bezpecne-prijdte-to-zjistit-do-oc-nisa.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902951-vite-zda-vase-dite-sedi-v-aute-skutecne-bezpecne-prijdte-to-zjistit-do-oc-nisa.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 17:56:00 +0200</pubDate><category>Doprava</category><description>Správně nainstalovaná autosedačka, správně usazené dítě a správně dotažené pásy – tři podmínky, které musí být splněny zároveň, aby autosedačka při nehodě plnila svou funkci. Přitom právě v těchto detailech rodiče nejčastěji chybují, aniž by o tom věděli.</description></item></channel></rss>

výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:23:12 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.3 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Podzimní hry 2026 – malá kopaná https://www.vybezek.eu/295858-podzimni-hry-2026-mala-kopana/ Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:23:12 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=295858 Ve středu 14. října 2026 se na umělém trávníku v areálu Kotliny ve Varnsdorfu uskutečnil druhý díl letošních podzimních her, tentokrát v malé kopané.

Turnaje se zúčastnila čtyři chlapecká družstva, která mezi sebou poměřila své síly systémem každý s každým. Jednotlivá utkání se hrála na 15 minut.

Naši chlapci vstupovali do turnaje s jasným cílem, kterým bylo obhájit prvenství z loňského roku. Hned v úvodním utkání proti ZŠ Východní předvedli výborný výkon a zaslouženě zvítězili vysoko 8:0. Ve druhém zápase je čekalo družstvo Gymnázia Varnsdorf. Díky skvělému vstupu do utkání a zodpovědnému výkonu si naši hráči připsali další přesvědčivé vítězství, tentokrát 4:0. V posledním utkání se naši chlapci utkali s družstvem ZŠ Edisonova. Přestože si během zápasu vytvořili řadu slibných brankových příležitostí, jejich neproměňování přineslo dramatickou koncovku. Nakonec však dokázali těsné vedení udržet a po vítězství 3:2 mohli slavit zasloužený triumf.

Naši fotbalisté tak prošli celým turnajem bez ztráty jediného bodu, s celkovým skóre 15:2, a úspěšně obhájili loňské prvenství!

Celý turnaj proběhl v přátelské a sportovní atmosféře. Všechna zúčastněná družstva si zaslouží pochvalu za předvedené výkony a nasazení. Našim chlapcům děkujeme za vzornou reprezentaci školy. Podzimní hry však pokračují dál. Již 3. 11. 2026 se uskuteční další díl, ve kterém žáci poměří své síly v plavání. Už teď se těšíme!

Mgr. Patrik Klouda, ZŠ Varnsdorf, nám. E. Beneše
